title: Bags for a South Bay day
dek: Court at seven, Trader Joe’s at ten, sand by two. Ten bags and one chair, sorted by the part of the day they’re for, with dated prices and honest catches.
heroAlt: A pixel-dithered specimen sheet of bags in black, cobalt and yellow: a pickleball backpack with two paddle handles, a canvas grocery tote with a baguette and flowers, a holey beach tote, a soft cooler with a can, a rope-strap sling, a duffel, a roll-top dry bag, pickleballs, a water bottle, keys on a carabiner, and a phone on a lanyard.
heroCredit: Illustration: Astra (Codex) for PointCast, after Mike Hoydich’s specimen sheets
method: Desk review from maker product pages, checked September 29, 2026, plus news coverage for the Trader Joe’s bag, which isn’t sold online. PointCast has not tested these bags. Picks are judged on fit for each moment of the day, size, materials, care and price; there is no star rating because nothing was handled.
disclosure: Every shopping link is a direct, non-affiliate link to the maker. PointCast earns no commission. Several of these brands run affiliate programs; we have not joined any of them. Prices are US list prices before tax and shipping.
endnoteTitle: Selkirk sling for the court. Baggu for the cart. Bogg for the sand.
verdict: If you buy three, buy those: $40, $16 and $90 cover most of a local day. Add the dry bag so your court clothes stop riding with the groceries. The YETI and the Helinox are nice to have, not the place to start.

moments.label: Court
moments.need: Paddle, balls, and somewhere for sweaty clothes.

moments.label: Trader Joe’s
moments.need: Stands up in the cart. Keeps frozen stuff cold on the drive.

moments.label: Beach
moments.need: Rinses off, lets sand out, and somewhere to sit.

moments.label: The car
moments.need: Cold drinks that can ride in the trunk for hours.

moments.label: Errands
moments.need: Hands free: phone, keys, a bottle.

moments.label: The trip
moments.need: Carry-on size. Shrugs off a wet dock.

picks.name: Core Line Sling Bag
picks.specs: Padded paddle pocket · bottle pocket to 24 oz · strap converts sling ↔ backpack
picks.review: Most mornings you carry one paddle, one ball, keys, a bottle. That’s this bag. It wears across the body walking in from the lot, the strap unzips into a backpack if you’re riding a bike, and a grab handle hangs it on the court fence instead of the ground.
picks.caveat: It fits one paddle, by Selkirk’s own description. No room for a backup or your partner’s.
picks.verdict: The everyday court bag. Start here.
picks.alt: Black Selkirk Core Line sling bag with a single shoulder strap and side mesh bottle pocket

picks.name: Vision II Backpack
picks.specs: Padded laptop sleeve · ventilated shoe partition · side mesh bottle pocket
picks.review: When court is on the way to or from work, you need more room. This one holds several paddles, a laptop in its own padded sleeve, and your shoes in a vented section of their own, so the work clothes don’t smell like the court.
picks.caveat: JOOLA doesn’t list capacity or weight, and the listed 2.0-inch depth can’t be right. See the size in person before you rely on it. The original Vision II listing is sold out; this is JOOLA’s current listing.
picks.verdict: Worth it if you play before or after work.
picks.alt: Black JOOLA Vision II pickleball backpack with a white JOOLA label on the front

picks.name: Evac Dry Bag, 13L
picks.priceNote: 13L shown. Sizes run 3L at $24.95 to 35L at $49.95; the 8L was out of stock on September 29.
picks.specs: Recycled 70D nylon · roll-top · taped seams · air-release base
picks.review: This is the pod nobody sells with a court bag. Wet shirt, damp socks and the towel go in, you roll the top, and nothing touches the car seat or the groceries. The base lets air squeeze out, so it packs flat.
picks.caveat: Because it’s waterproof, it also traps smell. Empty it when you get home, not tomorrow.
picks.verdict: The cheapest upgrade to any bag on this list.
picks.alt: A row of blue Sea to Summit Evac roll-top dry bags in six sizes

picks.name: Reusable Insulated Bag
picks.priceNote: Price on Trader Joe’s product page. The lime-green color is seasonal (August–October) and sold in stores only.
picks.specs: Padded walls · zippered insulated lid · over-the-shoulder straps · inside pocket
picks.review: The right cold bag for a Trader Joe’s run is the one they sell at the register. It fits a full frozen aisle, zips shut, and the straps go over your shoulder for the walk from the far end of the lot.
picks.caveat: You can only buy it in the store, and new colors sell out and get resold online at silly markups. If the lime green is gone, the standard colors do the same job.
picks.verdict: Buy two. Leave one in the trunk.
picks.sourceLabel: The Takeout on the lime-green bag
picks.alt: Illustration of a striped canvas grocery tote with a baguette and flowers, standing in for the Trader Joe’s bag
picks.credit: Illustration, not a product photo: Astra (Codex) for PointCast

picks.name: Standard Baggu
picks.specs: Recycled ripstop nylon · holds 50 lb · folds into a 5 × 5 in pouch · machine washable
picks.review: It holds what two or three plastic grocery bags would and folds into a pouch the size of your palm, so there’s always one in the glovebox. Throw it in the wash when the strawberries leak.
picks.caveat: It’s open at the top with no insulation. Groceries only; the frozen stuff goes in the bag above.
picks.verdict: The bag you’ll actually have with you.
picks.alt: Black Standard Baggu nylon shopping bag hanging flat

picks.name: Original Bogg Bag
picks.priceNote: $90 in solid colors; prints $100, licensed team bags $120.
picks.specs: EVA foam · stands on its own · 2 clear insert pouches · 3 lb empty
picks.review: Sand is the enemy of every other bag here, and this one doesn’t care. It stands up on its own, sand falls out through the holes, and you hose it off at the end of the day. The two clear pouches keep phone and keys out of the sunscreen.
picks.caveat: It weighs 3 lb empty and has no closure, so valuables sit in the open. Buy from boggbag.com: lookalike stores show up in search results, and returns close after 15 days with shipping on you.
picks.verdict: Worth $90 if you’re on the sand every weekend.
picks.alt: Mushroom-beige Original Bogg Bag, a molded tote with round holes and two handles

picks.name: Boat and Tote, Large
picks.priceNote: Large, regular handles. Medium $39.95; the line runs about $32.95–$59.95.
picks.specs: 24 oz cotton canvas · double-layer base · long-handle option · monogram
picks.review: It’s been sewn in Maine since 1944, and it wears in instead of out. It’s tall enough for a rolled towel and a thermos. It’s also the only bag here you’d monogram and hand down.
picks.caveat: Canvas soaks up water and wet sand, and the top is open. It’s a beach-parking-lot bag, not one to set down at the waterline.
picks.verdict: The one to buy if you want it to last twenty years.
picks.alt: Natural canvas L.L.Bean Boat and Tote with olive-green handles and base trim

picks.name: Chair One
picks.award: Best chair that packs like a bag
picks.specs: Aluminum frame · holds 320 lb · mesh panels · daisy-chain case · 5-year warranty
picks.review: A chair is part of the kit here: courtside while you wait, on the sand, at the park. Packed, this one is the size of a water bottle and clips onto any bag above by its case. It sets up in about the time it takes to find your sunglasses.
picks.caveat: The seat is only 9 inches off the ground, and the thin legs sink into soft sand. Helinox sells ball feet and a ground sheet to fix that, so a real beach setup costs more than $110.
picks.verdict: Best for the court and the park. Add the feet if it’s going to the sand.
picks.alt: Black Helinox Chair One with mesh panels on a blue aluminum frame

picks.name: Hopper Flip 12
picks.specs: DryHide shell · ColdCell foam · leakproof HydroLok zipper · wide flip-top
picks.review: This is the one bag that lives in the car. The leakproof zipper means melted ice doesn’t end up in the trunk carpet. It’s small enough to carry one-handed from the lot to the courts or the sand, and wide enough at the top to reach in without unpacking.
picks.caveat: It costs $250 for a 12-can-class cooler, and the 24-can figure assumes no ice. YETI’s page blocked our checker; we confirmed the price from YETI’s own product data and the specs from coverage quoting YETI.
picks.verdict: Buy it if you’ll use it every week. A cheaper soft cooler covers occasional use.
picks.alt: Charcoal YETI Hopper Flip 12 soft cooler with a shoulder strap

picks.name: Bottle Sacoche Medium
picks.priceNote: From $82 (bag only); most fabrics $92. The plaid wool shown is the fall 2026 edition. Straps are sold separately, from $38.
picks.specs: Bottle or umbrella sleeve · two zip compartments · key hook · Wares strap system
picks.review: This is the bag that made us want to write this. It’s small, with a sleeve for a 500 ml–1 L bottle and a key hook, and it clips onto Topologie’s interchangeable straps. You buy one strap, and every Topologie bag after that clips onto it. Phone, keys, a bottle, both hands free for a coffee and a dog leash.
picks.caveat: The strap isn’t included. The real price is about $120 or more, so budget for the strap on your first order.
picks.verdict: The best everyday sling on this list, once you add the strap.
picks.alt: Green plaid wool Topologie Bottle Sacoche Medium, a small zippered barrel bag

picks.name: Black Hole Duffel 40L
picks.specs: 100% recycled body, lining and webbing · TPU-film laminate · backpack straps · Ironclad Guarantee
picks.review: It’s carry-on size for most airlines, and the laminate shrugs off a wet dock, a truck bed or a sandy trunk. The shoulder straps stow when you don’t need them. When it wears out, Patagonia repairs it.
picks.caveat: 40 L is right for a weekend and tight for anything longer. The 55 L costs more but covers a week.
picks.verdict: The bag for the weekend trip.
picks.alt: Dark gray Patagonia Black Hole Duffel 40L with red handles and a blue Patagonia logo
